title: 3D Printing of In Vitro Hydrogel Microcarriers by Alternating Viscous-Inertial Force Jetting
protocol: Supplement high-glucose Dulbecco's modified Minimum Essential Medium (H-DMEM) with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS), 1% nonessential amino acid solution (NEAA), 1% penicillin G and streptomycin, and 1% Glutamine supplement.
Culture A549 cells in a CO2 incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Treat cells in the T75 culture flask with 3 mL of trypsin at approximately 80% confluence for 3 min.
Add 6 mL of culture medium to stop the trypsinization.
Pipette the culture medium to harvest loosely adhered cells.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 72.5 x g for 3 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend with 3 mL of fresh medium.
Transfer 1 mL of cell suspension to a new T75 culture flask containing 10 mL of fresh medium.
Change the culture medium every 2 days.
Load glass micropipettes onto the puller following the manufacturer's instructions.
Set pulling parameters for the puller: HEAT, PULL, VELOCITY, TIME, and PRESSURE are set to 560, 255, 255, 150, and 500, respectively.
Cut the nozzle at the designated diameter using a micro-forge device according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Locate the specified diameter of the nozzle onto the heated platinum wire.
Heat the wire up to 60 °C for about 5 seconds and pull the nozzle apart.
Immerse the printhead of the nozzle in a hydrophobic agent for 30 minutes.
Rinse the nozzle three times with sterilized water after immersing it in the hydrophobic agent.
Sterilize the nozzle in alcohol for 5 minutes before printing.
Rinse the nozzle three times with sterilized water to remove residual alcohol.
Dissolve NaCl (0.45 g) into 50 mL of sterile water to make a 0.9% (w/v) NaCl solution.
Vibrate the NaCl solution to promote dissolution.
Filter the dissolved NaCl solution through a 0.45 µm polyethylene terephthalate filter membrane.
Weigh low-viscosity sodium alginate powder (1 g) and dissolve it in 25 mL of the NaCl solution at high temperature (60-80 °C) overnight to obtain a 4% (w/v) sodium alginate stock solution.
Store the sodium alginate stock solution at 4 °C for up to one month.
Sterilize the sodium alginate stock solution by heating it three times in an oven (70 °C) for 30 minutes each time.
Dilute proper volume of sodium alginate stock solution in 0.9% NaCl solution at concentrations of 2%, 1.5%, and 0.5% (w/v).
Dissolve 1 g of gelatin powder in 25 mL of NaCl solution at a temperature of 60-80 °C overnight to obtain a 4% (w/v) gelatin stock solution.
Store the gelatin stock solution at 4 °C for up to 1 month.
Heat the gelatin stock solution three times in an oven at 70 °C for 30 minutes each time to sterilize it.
Dilute the proper volume of gelatin stock solution in 0.9% NaCl solution to achieve a concentration of 1.5% (w/v).
Mix the 2% (w/v) sodium alginate solution with the Type I collagen solution from rat tail at a ratio of 3:1.
Adjust the pH of the mixed solution to 7.2 using 0.1 M NaOH solution.
Dissolve tyrosine-modified HA flocculent solid in phosphate buffer saline (PBS) solution at 60-80 °C overnight to obtain a 0.8% w/w tyrosine-modified hyaluronic acid PBS solution.
Store the tyrosine-modified HA PBS stock solution at 4 °C for up to 1 month.
Heat the tyrosine-modified HA PBS solution three times in an oven at 70 °C for 30 minutes each time to sterilize it.
Dissolve horseradish peroxidase powder in PBS solution to obtain 8 enzyme activity unit/mg horseradish peroxidase PBS solution.
Dilute hydrogen peroxide solution with DI water to 4 mM.
Mix tyrosine-modified hyaluronic acid PBS solution and horseradish peroxidase PBS solution at a ratio of 1:1.
Sterilize the printing system by wiping with 75% (v/v) alcohol.
Expose the sterilized printing system to ultraviolet light overnight.
Use a home-established cell printing system as previously reported.
Amplify the electrical signal output by the waveform generator.
Drive piezoelectric ceramics to generate controllable deformation.
Produce controllable vibrations using the nozzle fixed on the piezoelectric ceramic.
Load 5 mL of bioink into a disposable sterile syringe.
Install the syringe on the syringe pump.
Connect the syringe and nozzle with a silicone hose of 1 mm inner diameter.
Fix the nozzle to be used for printing by adjusting the tightness of the clamping screw.
Wear thicker gloves if the nozzle is broken during installation.
Clean up glass fragments and residues carefully.
Push the syringe pump rapidly.
Load bioink to the nozzle.
Set flow rate at 30 µL/min.
Wipe off excess material at the tip.
Import self-designed waveform containing 500,000 sampling points.
Set sampling rate to 5 million samples/s.
Set peak-to-peak voltage (Vpp) to 10 V.
Clean slides or Petri dishes with deionized water.
Place them under the nozzle as printing substrate.
Preset motion path and trigger mode of vibration as drop-on-demand.
Print droplets following pre-designed patterns.
Dissolve 3 g of calcium chloride into 100 mL of sterile water to obtain 3% (w/v) calcium chloride solution.
Filter dissolved solution through a 0.45 µm polyethylene terephthalate filter membrane.
Add 5 mL of cross-linking solution into a Petri dish.
Place Petri dish under nozzle as substrate.
Cross-link microcarriers for 3 min after printing.
Collect microcarrier suspension in a centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the suspension at 29 x g for 3 min.
Resuspend the microcarriers in culture media at approximately 600 microcarriers/mL.
Remove culture media from A549 cells.
Add 5 mL of serum-free medium containing 10 µM Cell Tracker dye to the cells.
Incubate cells for 30 min in an incubator.
Replace the dye solution with fresh medium.
Resuspend the A549 cell suspension at a density of 1.6 x 10^6 cells/mL.
Add 1 mL of alginate-collagen microcarrier suspension to a low-adherent 6-well culture plate.
Add 1 mL of resuspended A549 cell suspension to the same well.
Place the plate onto a shaker at 30 rpm in an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Take the plate off the shaker and wait for 30 min.
Let the microcarriers settle down.
Half change the culture medium every 2 days.
Observe and measure the nozzle under a bright field microscope or confocal microscope.
Observe and measure Petri dishes under a bright field microscope or confocal microscope.
Observe and measure cells with microcarriers under a bright field microscope or confocal microscope.
Measure the diameter of the microcarriers by ImageJ software.
Set the actual size of the scale in ImageJ according to the scale bar from the microscope.
Draw 10 lines representing the radius or semi-major axis of the microcarriers.
Obtain the average size and standard deviation of these line segments.
